thread:
Yana: quick question - hitting flaky shutdowns with httpx.AsyncClient in our FastAPI app. pattern: create client at module scope, start a background task that polls, on reload/shutdown I see `Task was destroyed but it is pending!` and unclosed connection warnings. anyone seen this?
Matt: seen it. --reload + uvicorn lifespan ordering is messy. my workaround was to call `await client.__aenter__()` in startup and `await client.__aexit__()` on shutdown. works but feels gross.
Sarah: another option is anyio/uvicorn lifespan manager or using a dedicated daemon process for polls. fastapi.BackgroundTasks is request-scoped so won't help for process-level polling.
Yana: the __aenter__ trick helps locally but breaks in pytest + asyncio CI where tests run in different loops. we get "Event loop is closed" when aclose is awaited from a different loop.
Kevin: yup, we've had a test-race where a test creates client on loop A, then runner uses loop B and calls `client.aclose()` -> RuntimeError about scheduling on closed loop.
Matt: so two issues: (1) startup/shutdown ordering with uvicorn reloader, (2) cross-event-loop cleanup in tests. both lifecycle ergonomics.
devx-bot: ci: canary deploy finished (:white_check_mark:)
Sarah: small repro I used:
```
# startup
client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10)
await client.__aenter__()
async def poll_loop():
    try:
        while True:
            await client.get("/health")
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("poll cancelled")
```
On reload the task prints cancelled but client warns about unclosed connections.
Yana: right - connection pool not closed because aclose wasn't awaited in the same loop as the client was created.
Kevin: feature request: can SDK expose explicit `start()` and `stop()` async methods (in addition to context manager) so apps can `await client.start()` during startup and `await client.stop()` during shutdown? clearer than __aenter__ hack and avoids cross-loop implicitness.
Matt: also typing notes: `AsyncClient.__aenter__` is currently typed as Any in our stubs which confuses mypy. a typed `start()` that returns None and preserves self type would be great.
Sarah: +1 on docs. we should add a FastAPI + pytest snippet showing global AsyncClient lifecycle and safe cleanup. would've saved me time.
Yana: also seeing retry/auth noise - refresh token flow sometimes races during shutdown and spams 401s.
Kevin: that fits - if a background refresh runs while client is closing, retries get cancelled mid-flight and log noisy errors. SDK should cancel in-flight retries on stop.
Matt: I'll open an SDK issue with repro, typing request, and doc PR suggestion. linking here when done.
Yana: for now I'll guard aclose with `if not loop.is_closed()` and pin uvicorn to non-reload in CI. thanks!
Matt: created issue placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1234 — includes repro, request for `start()/stop()`, typing fix, and docs example.
Sarah: happy to pair on the docs snippet, ping me :wave:
Yana: pinged you, thanks :heart:
